title: Grateful Dead Live at Academy of Music on 1972-03-26
lineage: Dat (Sony D8) -> Samplitude Professional v9.11 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Apogee AD500 -> Dat (48k)

ai_review.summary: A superb soundboard remix that captures a high‑energy early‑'72 show with standout performances of Good Lovin', Looks Like Rain, Cold Rain & Snow and an incendiary Truckin’ → The Other One sequence.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑remixed SBD delivers crystal‑clear balance—Bob Weir front‑and‑center, Jerry Garcia’s pedal‑steel tone shining on Looks Like Rain, and a bright but clean piano from the newly introduced Keith.  Musically the night is fire‑breathing: an explosive Greatest Story opener, tight first‑set classics and a second set that builds into a monster Truckin’/The Other One jam, earning universal praise despite a few minor splice glitches and missing intro seconds.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive fan feedback (10 of 13 five‑star reviews) highlights both a high‑energy performance and an excellent‑to‑good soundboard mix; only isolated technical complaints lower the rating slightly.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, balanced SBD with Weir up front and a less recessed Garcia.  Minor splice/hiccup noted on Good Lovin' and missing first five seconds of Greatest Story; some listeners find the bright early‑'72 mix overly clean.

standout_songs: Truckin' → The Other One → Me & My Uncle → The Other One
show_quality.setlist_flow: A powerful opener with Greatest Story, a tight first set of classics, followed by an expansive second set that weaves extended jams and seamless transitions, culminating in a legendary Truckin'/The Other One sandwich.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Pedal‑steel tone on Looks Like Rain praised as magical; mix slightly less forward than on some releases but still strong.
band_member_comments.Phil: Provides lush harmonies on Looks Like Rain and is highlighted for his bass work throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm guitar and vocals are front‑center in the mix, especially on Good Lovin' and other early songs.
band_member_comments.Keys: New piano player Keith introduced during the set; his playing noted as solid and adds depth to the band’s sound.
band_member_comments.Drums: Solid drumming throughout; a notable single‑drummer feel on Not Fade Away is highlighted.
